Hi P,

I'd like to echo what Aaron said about the Forex Tester. It was the best $129 investment I've ever made. It will dramatically increase your learning speed. In a couple of hours you can test and evaluate your setups for what would have been months of real time. They are selling it for like $200 on their website right now, but I just googled for a coupon or discount and found a site that had a partnership with them and got it for $129. Based on what I've learned from it, I would have gladly paid the $200 in hindsight.

Whether you end up buying the program or not, keep studying and applying the teachings here and you will do fantastic. It just takes practice to train your eyes, but you will get it. For me it took several months before certain nuances began to click. I didn't even see those until I took a 2 month break from all things trading. When I came back with fresh eyes is when the clicks started to happen. For others it could take a few weeks or a few years. You'll know when you start seeing the market for what it is. It's like those digital garbled pictures that you have to stare off into space to see the picture. Everything is blurry with no rhyme or reason and you can't see it, and then when your eyes focus in the right spot the picture pops out at you clear as day. That's the best analogy I can think of.

Best of luck and know that you have support,

Mike

This is a visual representation of how I understand the movement of price

After I am done analyzing all 8 areas, I will then be using FT in live analysis in this journal. This analysis will be spread over 8 days... one for each day:)

Now looking into number 1 of the previous chart

Sorry for the blur... in the first chart the caption reads "Tries to get back in but fails, this is where price turns later" taken from w1

Here is the insert

Area 2

So now that I analyzed Area 1 and know that price broke into new historical highs, I am going to recap the move up from Area 1 into the new highs and what would have been the requirements to trade along the way.

First chart up is the monthly:

Here we clearly see that the up move started from Area 1 which was a FO to a monthly low as well as to a previous swing low on to its left. The confirmation that it was a FO came on this TF once we broke above the swing high between points 1 &2.

1- Here is the DBR, FO, QM & FTR, this will in the future be an excellent area to buy off of as is indicated by the arrow down pointing to Area 5. 2- After price broke the swing high (SH1) between 1 & 2, it flagged, broke the flag up into an FTR where it reacted creating another flag that also broke higher into the tip of the swing high 2 (SH2). There it retraced down to the local FL of the last break up before engulfing the SH2, it retraces creating another FL @ 3 & up it went. 3- This is the FL of the break of SH2 also some clear demand left there on this TF. Price between 3 & 2 is compressed and the only demand left is at the edges i.e. pts 3 & 2. 4- Price reaches prior highest historical high of the time & cuts right through that resistance creating the final FL of this TF before the RBD higher up. The supply below resistance @ 1.45350 was clearly consumed & if you notice that top is quite compressed. Also an important note is noticing the long wicked candles inside the yellow FL. They also imply lots of consumption of buy orders, not a great sign in case we wanted to buy that zone when price came back. 5- This is the area in focus and up till here in this TF I would want to see an engulf of the yellow FL for any shorts to take place. However, we know that as price moves it keeps on creating FLs and there’s one more I can see in here which is between the two bullish bars right under Area 2. It is marked with a “?” as we need to make sure it is a FL and also we need to define it.

Next chart is the D1, W1 didn’t show me much… So here I want to investigate and see first if the FL I pointed out to earlier with a “?” is in fact one. From the looks of it is.

But I want to look into its build up… So here is M30

From the monthly FL we see a buildup of many local FLs numbered 1 to 4. 4 being later a major area of support for the huge flag on top where a very big decision was then made to break higher. This zone has seen many FOs as it was being constructed. I am guessing that whenever something like this happens it only stretches the boundaries of a flag. Now we know that this area should hold price up when it comes back to it & if it breaks it would also be a great place to trade since it would flip polarities. So this becomes out next FL in line on the MN chart for a trade short after the break.

Back to daily

Here after we have defined our higher new MN FL in yellow we get a D1 local FL from which we could take the FTB which was also into D1 demand up to its origin at the last RBD supply.

Even thought a lot of seniors don’t advise to trade a FL area more than its FTB, I think they’ve mentioned that other setups in the zone are valid if PA confirms. So here I’ll show one other long setup from the same D1 FL but on H4

Finally before price moves out of our monthly/weekly base we get a very important heads up on what might be going on. A D1 FTR gets engulfed and unfortunately I do not see any opportunity to enter on smaller TFs… here’s the FTR

After that price breaks the D1 & MN FLs for the crash of 2008 while creating more FTRs which we could trade down from.

Price reaches Area 3 (which is our story for tomorrow:) ) but how does it stop where it did??? Well it reaches an old flag, and fakes it into SR/RS now support at around 1.23350

Be well RTM, see you all tomorrow

Area 3

The relevance of the broken lows at points 1, 2, & 3 are respectively associated with the breaks at A, B & C. Therefor on this TF they hold lots of weight compared to other ones that can be mostly considered local breaks.

Point 4 is as was discussed earlier the last FL before the big drop, thus the most important zone in this rally into Area 2.

The SR shows great history in several areas in the past, the most prominent one being the last time it acted as resistance before the big bullish candle that broke A (at X). The SR also shows lots of importance if we were to see it on a line chart.

When price broke down through all of 4, 3, 2, & 1, big NEW decisions were made along the way.

Now, I think there are two types of decisions in the market, prime & secondary. The former would be the break of something important like FL, FTR, Swing, SR, SD etc… & the latter the decision to either respect that initial decision (with a FL/FTR) or to reject it (with an Engulf of the primary in the opposite direction). Our job here at RTM is to follow in the footsteps of the last primary decision made until proven wrong (I think!!!), of course while bearing in mind all of what we have so generously been taught i.e. knowing where we are in terms of HTFs S/D and acting in our best interest.

As human beings first and traders second I believe our attention is drawn to chaos over harmony & clutter over order. The reason I say this is because I always seem to pick the wrong areas to trade from and suffer the consequences of this visual incompetence. In the following chart is an example;

In this chart we have the base of our previously discussed Area 2. In it I have highlighted the two most important FLs (IMHO) that were responsible for holding price up throughout this zone of balance. The upper green one bounced price back up 8 times as is seen on this TF. Now we know that the more a zone is visited the more orders get depleted from it especially if no newer orders are placed there. What I mean by that last part is, if you look at point A, this candle went really deep into the zone and must have picked up a lot of the remaining orders in the zone if not all of them. I for one would have definitely thought it would break down on the next visit after A… but it does not… why??? Because newer orders were placed there again. Be they limit or market orders… doesn’t matter… ITs bought there on two other occasions before finally breaking the green zone. So in other words, a zone is not broke b4 it is broke.

After the green price cuts through the yellow. Look at that beauty of a WRB! Nice! Had this been real time I am not even sure I would have given the yellow importance over the green… I know I wouldn’t have! Why look at all the action that took place in the green, isn’t this the area to look for a juicy short for when & if price comes back… surely! …. WRONG!!! First price doesn’t make it there, second, hell if I was an IT why would I want to sell in an obvious place such as the green? So I’m slowly coming to the conclusion that the most important areas could be those we pay very little attention to like the yellow one.

Here’s the return to it

Excuse my delay on the initial analysis of Area 3… back into it now… So the last thing we were discussing was the new decisions made on the way down. Here they are;

Price breaks A & B retraces at 1 & goes lower making 1 a W1 FTR

Price then breaks C retraces up to 2 where it reacts very strongly because of 1 and continues down to D. In the process the continuation of price through point X makes 2 another W1 FTR.

Down to daily for a clearer view on the rest

Price breaks D makes a low at Z retraces up to Y and then it’s back on the way down through Z into E. Making 3 a FL with an FTR at Y. Price halts at the SR back from the first chart. Now we also see that the latest FL gets engulfed north signaling opposition. This one goes back to 3 as an FTB and we could have traded the return into confirmed demand in 4 once price came back targeting Y. Entering is one thing, holding is another… I don’t think I would have had the patience before starting to second guess myself as this is often the case.

Price then engulfs the FL at 3 & the FTR at Y, reaches ultimate target which is the second W1 FTR and drops as expected. Let’s see if I could get an entry…

Price engulfs the last FL on the way up, creates a flag (around our previous low C from chart 4) and breaks another important zone before returning to give a chance at 1. The approach into 1 is a weak one as is evident.

Stop would be above the zone of the flipped FL

This would be target… next zone in line on H4

Entry would be on M15 after the ENG and on RT to line C (previous SR)

We then make it to target and beyond into the source of the move that rallied all the way up to the second W1 FTR… A second visit to Area 3 (to be continued in a while…. Sorry I need a break )

Area 3 – Continued

Ok a little recap on the target…

Had I looked better Target should have been lower. Here is the chart;

On the left we have the FL from post #34 Chart # 5 with an upper limit (FTR) Y & a lower limit Z. Zone A was the decision that was made to break the lower limit. And when price came back there it gave us the FTB to the FL at B. Then at C price broke through that decision “A” creating another FL. This should have been target! That was like an extra 420 pips… Now why C not D??? Simple really, because the FL at D wasn’t important in itself since it did not break something major. Had I chosen E instead as a target I think I would have gotten a passing grade! Ok … In the same way C is important, E is very important because it broke the yellow FL on the left & FTR Y. So now a break of E and or C becomes significant... They both break and result in the creation of new important prime and secondary decisions.

Here we clearly see both breaks of E & C with their respective FTRs marked as FTR1 & FTR2 followed by their FTBs pointed to in white arrows. Now when price broke through FL C it got to the upper part of the base of the last DBR and started to react to demand there. It came to FTR2 and went back down consuming more long orders from previous untested demand zones. As it was dipping into the base it was also removing lots of sell orders as is evident in the compressed tops. It reaches the final untested demand before curling up and heading into FTR1.

For some the CP action is enough to get them in a position, I’d rather get it confirmed…

There are three ways a position could have been entered as I see it

1- Based on a FO of a D1 low with a PO at the green horizontal line after the candle “a” breaks the low & closes above. A fill would have come in the following day at “b” with stops below the zone of the untested demand. BUT that is an entry for the brave and since I am not I drop lower…

2- A second option would be once price came back to the source of the ENG move on H4, which was a FTR on H1 entry.

3- The final option which I would chose, the FTR setup on H4 with a white arrow pointing to where I’d try to get in. In all three cases the stop would be the same below the zone of the untested demand.

I would have definitely tried to hold until reaching FTR1 of the D1 chart. Granted I would have been a little nervous approaching the last supply of the CP, but by then I should have been well in the black and safe to wait it out i.e. engulfing into CP.

**This is taking much longer than I thought it would… will have to put off the rest until later.

Be well,

Finishing off Area 3

Price gets to FTR1 engulfs south giving entry opportunity after it retraces into the source of the engulf and also D1 supply. Keeps going until reaching pole1 for a second visit (V2). It bounces up to Local FTR and back down deeper into Pole1 from which point it goes to pick up the orders left at the FTR TO ENG2. From there price heads back down breaking POLE1 @ ENG3 into the next FTR in line fakes it into Demand of the flag @ Pole2. Since this was the origin of the move up that had broken into CP, it is from this point that all the big buyers come back in to take price higher up. Now that FTR1 has had most of its orders removed, it shouldn’t constitute much of a hurdle when price gets there again. But nothing is for certain b4 it gets taken. If it does the next one up would be the base of the drop prior to FTR1.

As we had expected price doesn’t find it very hard to break up into FTR1 creating the yellow FL that will be a very important factor in floating price up in a huge flag all the way until it reaches destination or AREA4.

AREA 4

For argument’s sake and for my sanity I am going to assume that I am an astute trader who was expecting a reaction at the yellow monthly flipped FL from Area 2 & not waiting for price to get to the “visually impaired” zone in green above it.

Here we see that price keeps on going until it reaches Area 4 while cutting through the hurdles on the way (FTR2 & FTR3) which had already been tested previously in the analysis post # 34. But right above FTR3 there remained one more on H4/D1 with its high at the red dashed horizontal line… Going lower to define it, maybe it could turn price.

Now that it’s defined I wanna see if there was any supply left there… down to M5

This RBD was in reaction to a previous decision (not shown here) to break yet another FL that was just below our yellow one from Area 2. The white Xs point to areas where price backed up on itself i.e. the only place that could turn price could be the very top base above the first green horizontal line. I’m gonna extend that into the future with the SR n see what happens when price comes back into it.. if anything…

Check this out yes it does react and right at the SR of the M5 RBD base.

At this point I really don’t know whether it is going to go higher… but what I do have is the beautiful reaction off of H4 and entry opportunity arises when price comes back into the source of the drop @ 2. Some would have been able to trade the CP down at the first touch of the zone @ 1… but I’m not there yet. I will drill down chose a place to put a PO with SL above the source and TP at FTA on the TF I put the PO.

So I chose my entry & target based off of SR… not a good RR barely a 1:1… I NEED to STUDY HARDER!!!

This was why I chose the bottom of the zone

During this time price is bouncing back and forth between the two light blue zones until it decides to break north taking out the last standing FTR at the red dotted horizontal line. Touches the MN flipped FL and dives, engulfing a nice FTR on this TF. Probably worth a shot down if price comes back up… Looking lower for a plan.

When price broke through the H4/D1 FTR at the red line we got a nice FL up. Right there on the red line a decision was made to break the upper limit of the FL. This is where I will place a PO to sell at 1.50830 with stop above the top and a first target at the origin of the move back up i.e. around green FTR.

I will not get nervous, I will stick to my plan… this is higher TF and so if and when T1 is reached I will take off 2/3 and let 1/3 run until price says otherwise.

I get a fill and price keeps rising for a couple of days before falling like a stone. Throughout the fill I am in drawdown and close to being stopped out. Luckily I am not! T1 is reached and 1/3 is still open. I will close when I see an opposite engulf on H1 (Has to be non-local), then I will wait for a retrace and maybe get out at a better price.

This is my exist after the engulfs on H1and a RT down to the red SR.

This trade was a much better one even though it might have stressed me out in the beginning. The approximate RRs were 2.4 & 9.5 on the first & second portions of the trade. So yes much better!

Looking at the big picture again and as we had discussed earlier in the last part of post #36, this yellow FL is very important and had I had the guts I should have held the previous trade until there! So looking lower for a seat to take me there especially that these lows look compressed on this TF

I am gonna place a PO on the D1 FL lower limit around 1.45859 (marked with a tick) and a SL just above 1.46850 (marked with an x). First immediate target would be the green QM level and of the zone there.

And NO FILL! Misses by 8 pips without the spread… But reaches target nicely… What the hell did I do wrong?!

Like the moron that I am I did not check lower, just went for the OBVIOUS area AGAIN! If you look at the chart you’ll see that my entry level had already been tested a while back at 1 and thus created a newer zone I had completely missed! I looked deeper into it and to be honest did not see how I could have traded that especially that it was a local zone. I just don’t see it… If someone could help me out here it would be great…

*** Taking a little break

Hope everyone is having a good Sunday:)

Area 5

Because I made my homework I knew I should expect some kind of reaction at this level. I couldn’t know that for sure until it did react (that is something I am drilling into my head).

Just look at the history of this SR/QM level! Notice the orange arrows in the past there. There was some serious buying.

Point A is the low of 2008 i.e. the lowest point price got to during the crash of that year.

Point B is the low of 2009, and as is clear during the beginning of that year when price came into the zone of the low of A, there were buyers. Why? Because it was last year’s low zone from which point price rallied, so people bought again. Isn’t’ that text book herd behavior? When price visits those levels again what is the expectation of the ITs? They’ll know that there surely will be buyers around those levels following the “buy low, sell high” advice no? Also wouldn’t there be break out traders salivating over price going down to hell? Surely…

What happens next is buyers & sellers get tripped for their stops, the ITs fill their huge orders and price rallies. This can be clearly seen through the candles 1,2 & 3.

On this TF we also see that the drop in A cleared all the demand down to A, engulfing the previous FTR at X which implies that SHOULD (not a necessity) price ever cross below A it will go down to the next FTR in line. I like to look for clean, clear, untested preferably non-local FTRs.

Now price keeps going until it hits a wall of buyers around our QM level. If I were to be strictly trading this TF I would need C to get taken out of the way before considering buying.

Here are the FTRs in line and they all fall inside our bigger zone from weekly. The middle one I did not project it into the future as it had already been tested pointed to with an orange arrow. So watching PA there on nothing less than D1 TF is the safest since a lot of chop can happen before a decision is taken. Once a decision has been made on D1 and I can clearly see that only then will I start going lower.

Here we see price cuts through the previous yearly lows B & A, hesitates a little then drops into FTR1, bounces from there up to the supply where the decision (also a FL area) was made to break into B & A, creates area C now also a FTR (same C from previous chart) and goes back down to FTR1 where again a lot of buy and sell orders are being exchanged (In another life I would be stuck in this chop!). After the ENG it was decided that price will in fact go lower. The deciding factors here are the move beyond the lower limit of the ENG, the break of FTR1 and the close of that WRB below the level. The following day price drops into FTR2 (which is also a combinations of other things pointed to in the first chart) and starts a slow move up. At this point I still don’t know anything for sure but by just looking four days into the touch of FTR2 the story says a lot. The first two candles show the sellers lost the upper hand (maybe just for a short while), on the third day the demand in the second candle was revisited (look at the lower wick) also it had a long upper wick and a small body (green none the less). That upper wick indicates that at some point during the day there was buyer power and lots of it only to get overcome by sellers. Could the following day continue lower then… possibly… but no the fourth day confirms the presence of big buyers and that the previous day’s high wick was consumption of sellers.

At this point I am still not interested in touching this; I want to see a break of the yellow FL. And it comes a few days later… great now lower!

Inside the daily FL the decision “Y” that had been taken to break out of the lower limit and FTR1 is now very clear. Y was also the lowest high on the curve before the lowest low. When price got back there on the way up it flagged, then decided to break into the zone of Y & out of it. There wasn’t really any respect shown to such a big decision. After that price created a FL/FTR @ Z.

The plan is the following: IF and when price comes back into the zone of Z or lower into the Demand that broke the lower flag up I will watch for buyers.

Buyers do show and I set a PO at the QM with a SL behind the rectangle at Y & a TP1 at T1 & T. Knowing full well that if the trade ever makes it that far it could go beyond into C from weekly.

Price comes close no fill for me but the QM worked from its demand, price goes to T1(FTR by the way). I’m upset for sure! Ok… I remove order and wait again…

Price comes back and strong, goes deep into the area of Y even breaks Z now, I’m starting to think I might be wanting to long when in fact maybe we’re going much lower. Price broke Swing Low 2 (SL2), SL1 & Z. So unless I see some sign of buying there will be not buying before the Green rectangles & even then I want proof (Engulfing or CP).

THERE IS BUYING! The last two seller decisions have been countered and I go on to place a PO. This time it will be around the top edge of rectangle Y at 1.22130… it just looks like a good SR… SL & TP1 will still be the same as before except now that point T1 has had so many tests T is first in line.

Price reaches TP1 I take 2/3 out. The next sign will be an engulf in the opposite direction on H1. That comes in around C from weekly and a strong drop happens, I just close and run… RR were app 3.2 & 5.7… not bad

Will wait out the chop to see what happens… back higher
